source.author: hor
source.text: atqui si vitiis mediocribus ac mea paucis mendosa est natura, alioqui recta, velut si egregio inspersos reprendas corpore naevos, si neque avaritiam neque sordes nec mala lustra obiciet vere quisquam mihi, purus et insons, ut me collaudem, si et vivo carus amicis, causa fuit pater his; qui macro pauper agello noluit in Flavi ludum me mittere, magni quo pueri magnis e centurionibus orti laevo suspensi loculos tabulamque lacerto ibant octonos referentes Idibus aeris, sed puerum est ausus Romam portare docendum artis quas doceat quivis eques atque senator semet prognatos.
source.text_original: atqui si vitiis mediocribus ac mea paucis  / mendosa est natura, alioqui recta, velut si  / egregio inspersos reprendas corpore naevos,  / si neque avaritiam neque sordes nec mala lustra  / obiciet vere quisquam mihi, purus et insons,   / ut me collaudem, si et vivo carus amicis,  / causa fuit pater his; qui macro pauper agello  / noluit in Flavi ludum me mittere, magni  / quo pueri magnis e centurionibus orti  / laevo suspensi loculos tabulamque lacerto  / ibant octonos referentes Idibus aeris,  / sed puerum est ausus Romam portare docendum  / artis quas doceat quivis eques atque senator  / semet prognatos.
source.text_english: And yet, if my character is blemished by moderate faults and a few defects, otherwise upright, as if you were to criticize moles sprinkled on a fine body, if no one can rightly charge me with greed or meanness or disgraceful debaucheries, pure and guiltless as I am, so that I may praise myself, if I am also dear to my friends while alive, my father was the cause of these things. Though poor with a small farm, he would not send me to the school of Flavius, where great boys, the sons of great centurions, hung with purse and tablet on the left arm, used to go, each carrying eight bronze coins on the Ides; but he dared to take his son to Rome to be taught the arts that any knight or senator would teach their own children.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: nam uitiis nemo sine nascitur; optimus ille est, qui minimis urguetur, uelut si egregio inspersos reprehendas corpore naeuos.
reuse.text_original: nam uitiis nemo sine nascitur; optimus ille est, qui minimis urguetur, uelut si egregio inspersos reprehendas corpore naeuos.
reuse.text_english: For no one is born without faults; he is the best who is pressed by the fewest, just as if you were to blame moles sprinkled on an excellent body.
